title: Solve Subject–Verb Agreement with the Odd-One-Out Trick
description: Use the he-or-they test to recognize a singular-versus-plural verb pattern, choose the one answer that differs from the other three, and avoid using the shortcut on verb-tense questions.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep your first idea, even if you are unsure. You can continue without submitting an answer.

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html:
In 1911, a university expedition crossed the high plateau collecting alpine plants. The collection of field notebooks, sketches, and pressed specimens assembled by the expedition's two botanists ______ now housed in the university's herbarium, where conservators recently began digitizing it. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

  1. are
  2. is
  3. were
  4. have been

blocks.html:
Start with the choices

The long opening sentence has details you may not need for this shortcut. We can start with its answer choices instead.

We’ll learn the he/they test and the eligibility checks for choosing the odd one out. First, practise with shorter choices.

Try both frames

Test “is studying,” “study,” “have studied,” and “are studying” after “he” and after “they.” Which one fits a different frame from the other three?

content.prompt: Which answer behaves differently after he and they?
content.hint: Say each full phrase aloud after he, then after they. Three fit they; one fits he.
content.explanation: He is studying works, while they study, they have studied, and they are studying work. The first answer is the singular odd one out.

blocks.html:
Recognize the three-to-one pattern

The eligible SAT pattern has three choices that fit one frame and one choice that fits the other. The Odd-One-Out shortcut selects that different choice. The eligibility checks are part of the method.

Use “he” and “they” as frames

A singular form fits “he”: “he inspires.” A plural form fits “they”: “they inspire.” Test the actual words in both frames to classify a choice.

content.prompt: Which phrase fits after they but not after he?
content.hint: Say the full phrase after they. Then check whether it also works after he.
content.explanation: They inspire works, but he inspire does not. The other three choices fit after he.

blocks.html:
Keep the whole choice together

“He has discovered” and “he is discovering” fit the singular frame. “They have discovered” and “they are discovering” fit the plural frame. Test the complete phrase, including its helping verb.

content.prompt: How should you classify have transformed?
choices: Singular, because the phrase he have transformed sounds correct.
Neither, because the choice contains two separate words.
Both singular and plural, depending on the sentence around it.
Plural, because they have transformed works and he have transformed does not.
content.hint: Try the complete phrase after both testing words.
content.explanation: They have transformed works; he have transformed does not. The phrase is plural.

blocks.html:
Check when the shortcut works

  1. All four choices are complete verbs or verb phrases.
  2. Each fits “he” or “they,” never both or neither.
  3. The split is three to one.

If a condition fails, use a different verb strategy.

content.prompt: Which answer set is safe for the odd-one-out trick?
choices: develops; develop; are developing; have developed
is developing; are developing; has developed; have developed
content.hint: Every choice must fit exactly one of he or they, and the final split must be three to one.
content.explanation: Develops fits he; the other three fit they. In the second set, developed fits both. In the third, developing fits neither. The fourth set splits two and two.

blocks.html:
Run the Odd-One-Out routine

  1. Scan the complete verb choices.
  2. Test each after “he” and “they.”
  3. Check all eligibility conditions.
  4. Choose the form in the minority.

One singular choice

“They are restoring,” “they restore,” and “they have restored” work. “He restores” works. Three fit “they” and one fits “he,” so “restores” is the odd one out.

content.prompt: Which answer is the singular odd one out?
content.hint: Try he before each complete answer. Only one will work.
content.explanation: He documents works. The other three choices fit after they.

blocks.html:
The pattern can reverse

“He supports,” “he has supported,” and “he is supporting” work. Only “they support” fits the other frame. With a three-to-one split, “support” is the odd one out.

content.prompt: Which answer is the plural odd one out?
content.hint: Three choices fit after he. Find the one that fits after they.
content.explanation: They influence works, while the other three choices fit after he.

blocks.html:
Use the shortcut once the checks pass

When the choices meet every eligibility condition, use their three-to-one pattern. You do not need to hunt through the sentence for the subject as an extra step in this shortcut.

content.prompt: This answer set passes the eligibility gate. Which choice is the odd one out?
content.hint: The first three fit after they. Which one fits after he?
content.explanation: Shapes is the singular odd one out. You did not need the sentence.

blocks.html:
What if a choice fits both?

“He walked” and “they walked” both work. That choice cannot be classified into just one frame, so the shortcut is ineligible. Switch to a different verb strategy for the sentence.

content.prompt: How should you classify discovered?
choices: Fits the he frame, but not the they frame
Fits the they frame, but not the he frame
Fits both the he and they frames
Fits neither the he nor they frame
content.hint: Try both: he discovered; they discovered.
content.explanation: Both frames work, so discovered is not exclusive. A choice like this blocks the shortcut.

blocks.html:
What if a choice fits neither?

“He cataloging” and “they cataloging” are both incomplete. A bare “-ing” form fails the eligibility check. “Is cataloging” and “are cataloging” can be tested normally as complete phrases.

content.prompt: Which choice is neither singular nor plural because it is not a complete verb by itself?
content.hint: Try placing each entire choice after both he and they.
content.explanation: Neither he recording nor they recording works. The standalone -ing form blocks the shortcut.

blocks.html:
Test the word instead of rejecting all past forms

“He was” and “they were” separate cleanly. Past tense by itself does not close the shortcut. The test is whether each actual choice fits exactly one frame.

content.prompt: Which choice is the singular odd one out, making this set eligible for the shortcut?
content.hint: Try each complete choice after he and they. Three fit they; one fits he.
content.explanation: Was fits he; were, are, and have been fit they. Every choice fits exactly one frame, so the three-to-one set is eligible.

blocks.html:
A two-to-two split has no odd answer

“Is” and “has been” fit “he”; “are” and “have been” fit “they.” Every choice fits one frame, but the split is two to two. The shortcut is ineligible.

content.prompt: When is the odd-one-out shortcut safe?
choices: Whenever the four choices contain verbs, even if one of them fits both he and they.
Whenever at least one of the four choices ends in the letter -s.
Only when every choice is exclusively singular or plural and the split is three to one.
Only after you identify the complete subject of the sentence.
content.hint: Retrieve both parts of the gate: exclusive classification and one odd answer.
content.explanation: Every answer must fit one—and only one—of the testing frames, and exactly one answer must differ from the other three.

shared_prompt.title: Maps and field journals sentence
shared_prompt.html: The collection of maps, together with several handwritten field journals, ___ how rapidly the coastline changed.

content.prompt: Which choice completes the sentence?
content.hint: Three choices fit after they. Find the one that fits after he.
content.explanation: Reveals is the singular odd one out. The nearby plural nouns never needed to enter your decision.

shared_prompt.title: Distant stars sentence
shared_prompt.html: New measurements of the distant stars, despite the limits of the original instruments, ___ the research team's conclusion.

content.prompt: Which choice completes the sentence?
content.hint: The first three fit after he. Which one fits only after they?
content.explanation: Support is the plural odd one out, so it is correct.

blocks.html:
Recognize a set that fails the checks

For “The laboratory ___ the samples last night,” compare “analyzed,” “has analyzed,” “will analyze,” and “analyzes.” Some fit both frames. That closes the shortcut, even though all four choices are verbs.

content.prompt: What should you do with the laboratory question?
choices: Choose analyzes, because it is the one choice ending in -s.
Choose analyzed because past tense is always singular.
Use the odd-one-out trick after finding the nearest noun.
Do not use the shortcut; the choices are not exclusively singular or plural.
content.hint: Test analyzed and will analyze after both he and they.
content.explanation: He analyzed and they analyzed both work; so do he will analyze and they will analyze. The eligibility gate fails.

blocks.html:
Check this question before choosing a method

Test the complete choices after “he” and “they.” Studies, has been studying, and was studying fit “he” only. Will study fits both frames.

Eligibility: A choice fits both frames, so this answer set is ineligible for Odd-One-Out.

With the gate closed, read the sentence for its time clues. Use them to answer the question on the next card.

shared_prompt.title: Bonnie Buratti’s discovery
shared_prompt.html:
Bonnie Buratti of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory ______ data about Saturn’s rings collected by the Cassini spacecraft when she made an interesting discovery: the tiny moons embedded between and within Saturn’s rings are shaped by the buildup of ring material on the moons’ surfaces.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

  1. studies 

  2. has been studying

  3. will study

  4. was studying

shared_prompt.title: Bonnie Buratti’s discovery
shared_prompt.html: Bonnie Buratti of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory ______ data about Saturn’s rings collected by the Cassini spacecraft when she made an interesting discovery: the tiny moons embedded between and within Saturn’s rings are shaped by the buildup of ring material on the moons’ surfaces.

content.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
content.hint: The shortcut is ineligible. Look at “when she made an interesting discovery.” When was the studying happening?
content.solution: “When she made” places the discovery in the past. The studying was ongoing when that discovery occurred, so the past progressive “was studying” fits: D. “Studies” is present, “has been studying” connects past activity with the present, and “will study” is future. The eligibility check correctly signaled that this question needs tense reasoning.
content.explanation: “Was studying” places the ongoing study at the time of the past discovery. The eligibility check sent you to the sentence’s time relationship.

content.prompt: Which choice makes this answer set ineligible because it fits neither he nor they?
content.hint: Try each entire choice after both he and they. One choice cannot complete either frame.
content.explanation: Documenting alone is not a complete verb, so it fits neither frame and makes the set ineligible. Is documenting is a complete singular phrase.

blocks.html:
Return to the expedition’s collection

Try the opening question again. Use the he/they frames and check every eligibility condition before choosing the odd one out.

content.prompt: Return to the opening question. What answer do you get now?
content.hint: Test each complete choice after he and after they. Check that every choice fits exactly one frame and the split is three to one.
content.explanation: The subject is the singular "collection" — the notebooks, sketches, specimens, and botanists are all inside interrupting phrases. In the frames, "is" fits "he" while "are," "were," and "have been" fit "they": a three-to-one split, so the odd one out wins.
content.solution: The subject is the singular "collection" — the notebooks, sketches, specimens, and botanists are all inside interrupting phrases. In the frames, "is" fits "he" while "are," "were," and "have been" fit "they": a three-to-one split, so the odd one out wins.

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html: In 1911, a university expedition crossed the high plateau collecting alpine plants. The collection of field notebooks, sketches, and pressed specimens assembled by the expedition's two botanists ______ now housed in the university's herbarium, where conservators recently began digitizing it. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

content.prompt: A verb question with four choices. From memory: how do you run the odd-one-out test, and what has to be true before you're allowed to?
choices: Test every choice after he and they; continue only if the split is two to two; choose the answer that sounds correct after they.
Test every choice after the closest noun; continue only if each fits exactly one; choose the answer that matches the noun's number.
Test every choice after he and they; continue whenever at least one choice fits both; choose the answer that differs.
Test every choice after he and they; continue only if each fits exactly one and the split is three to one; choose the answer that differs.
content.explanation: You have it: he or they, exactly one, three to one, choose the different answer.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

shared_prompt.title: Architects sentence
shared_prompt.html: The influence of the two architects, visible in the building's curved walls and open courtyards, ___ later designers throughout the region.

content.prompt: Which choice completes the sentence?
content.explanation: Has inspired is the singular odd one out. Once the three-to-one split appeared, the sentence could not distract you.

content.prompt: Which set should make you stop and use a different verb strategy?
choices: has changed; change; are changing; have changed
predicts; predict; are predicting; have predicted
content.explanation: Predicted fits both he and they, so that set fails the eligibility gate. Each of the other sets creates a clean three-to-one split.

content.html:
The Odd One Out

He or they, then check the split. Use the shortcut only when every eligibility condition passes.
